_PLOT_LOCK (threading.Lock) serialises figure creation/saving/closing: FastMCP 4.0.3 runs sync tools in an anyio worker thread (fastmcp/tools/function_tool.py:477 call_sync_fn_in_threadpool) and pyplot state is process-global; dc.pl.obsm calls plt.close() on the current figure. parameters.group_key: required (brief); tutorial 'condition'; must exist in obs, else ValueError
parameters.min_count/min_total_count/large_n/min_pr: 10/15/10/0.7 = tutorial cells 11/13 values = upstream API defaults
parameters.not_exposed: lib_size (API param, not used by tutorial; scalar library size rarely meaningful), inplace (tool always writes the filtered object)

plot saved via upstream Plotter save= (bbox_inches='tight')
decoupler_filter_genes_by_expression.outputs: filtered_counts.h5ad (obs kept, X subset), filter_by_expr_thresholds.png; summary n_samples, n_genes_before/after/removed, group_sizes, parameters
decoupler_filter_genes_by_expression.deviations: none in computation; no separate kept-gene list file (var_names of the h5ad hold it).

pydeseq2_test_differential_expression.signature: (data_path: str, condition_key: str, group: str, reference: str, design: str | None = None, n_cpus: int = 8, output_dir: str | None = None) -> dict

upstream_calls.call: DeseqStats(dds, contrast=[condition_key, group, reference], inference=inference, quiet=True)
dc.pl.volcano(data=results_df, x='log2FoldChange', y='padj', top=10, return_fig=True, save=<png>)

parameters.condition_key/group/reference: required; tutorial 'condition'/'treatment'/'control' -> user metadata (runtime.md metadata-input rule)
parameters.design: default f'~{condition_key}' (tutorial '~condition'). pydeseq2 0.5.4 accepts formulaic strings: dds.py L295-299 builds FormulaicContrasts(self.obs, self.design) for str designs; dev check: '~batch + condition' -> variables {batch, condition}, design columns [Intercept, batch[T.b2], batch[T.b3], condition[T.treatment]]
parameters.n_cpus: 8 (tutorial DefaultInference(n_cpus=8)); executor showed n_cpus=1 and 8 give bitwise-identical results
parameters.fixed: refit_cooks=True (tutorial); all other PyDESeq2 defaults (alpha 0.05, cooks_filter, independent_filter)

input_validation: condition column must not be numeric/boolean (PyDESeq2 would treat it as continuous)
group != reference; both must be levels of obs[condition_key] (error lists available levels)
counts finite, non-negative, integer-valued (PyDESeq2's own precondition, utils.py::test_valid_counts::110); reported, never repaired
design must include condition_key (checked via dds.variables before the expensive fit)
io_adaptations: adata.copy() passed to DeseqDataSet (executor: PyDESeq2 shares/mutates .uns and breaks later h5ad writes)
quiet=True on DeseqDataSet and DeseqStats: in the installed source it only gates print() calls (summary() prints results_df to stdout, which would corrupt MCP stdio); computation unchanged
sparse X densified (PyDESeq2 expects dense counts)
results_df.to_csv(path) keeps the gene index as first column (index name as produced by PyDESeq2, i.e. unnamed)
pydeseq2_test_differential_expression.outputs: deseq2_results.csv (baseMean, log2FoldChange, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj), deseq2_volcano.png; summary design, contrast, samples_per_level, n_genes, n_missing per column, n_padj_lt_0.05 (+up/down), top_up/top_down (5 each), pydeseq2_version

decoupler_score_activities_ulm.signature: (de_results_path: str, network: Literal['collectri','progeny','hallmark'], stat_column: str = 'stat', contrast_name: str | None = None, padj_threshold: float = 0.05, barplot_top: int | None = None, dotplot_top: int = 10, network_path: str | None = None, output_dir: str | None = None) -> dict

upstream_calls.call: dc.pl.barplot(data=sig_acts, name=row, top=preset_or_user, figsize=preset, return_fig=True, save=<png>)

df = sig_acts.melt(value_name='score').merge(padj.melt(value_name='padj').assign(clip(2.22e-16,1)).assign(-log10)); dc.pl.dotplot(df, x='score', y='variable', s='padj', c='score', top=dotplot_top, scale=preset, figsize=preset)

parameters.network: required Literal; organism fixed 'human' (non-human deferred by scanner)
parameters.contrast_name: None -> row label stays the stat column name (untransformed results_df[[stat]].T); tutorial used 'treatment.vs.control', pass it to reproduce reference tables exactly
parameters.barplot_top: None -> tutorial value: 25 CollecTRI (cell 34) / 25 PROGENy (cell 44) / 10 Hallmark (cell 56)
parameters.dotplot_top: 10 (cell 58 top=10; cell 46 uses the dotplot default, also 10)

input_validation: de_results_path exists; gene index unique/non-missing; stat_column present and numeric
stat_column must be finite for all genes (ulm asserts finite input); error suggests filtering genes, nothing dropped silently
network table must have source/target columns
io_adaptations: DE results read from the CSV written by tool 3 (composition contract)
network_path (CSV/TSV/Parquet) replaces the download when given
network table actually used is written as <network>_network_used.csv
decoupler_score_activities_ulm.outputs: <net>_ulm_scores.csv (wide, all sources, = native ulm scores), <net>_ulm_padj.csv (wide, all sources), <net>_ulm_scores_significant.csv (tutorial's filtered acts), <net>_network_used.csv, barplot and dotplot PNGs (only when >=1 significant source); summary network_origin/rows/n_sources, n_sources_scored, n_significant (+pos/neg), top_significant_sources and top_sources_all (5 each sign)
deviations: CollecTRI dotplot is not in the tutorial; it uses the cell-46 (PROGENy) dotplot settings (scale 0.15, figsize (4,4)), as the brief requested a dotplot for the tool.
When no source passes padj_threshold, bar/dot plots are skipped (upstream barplot cannot plot an empty frame) and the message says so.

decoupler_inspect_source_targets.signature: (de_results_path: str, network: Literal['collectri','progeny','hallmark'], source: str, stat_column: str = 'stat', scores_path: str | None = None, network_sources: list[str] | None = None, network_path: str | None = None, output_dir: str | None = None) -> dict

upstream_calls.call: dc.pl.volcano(data=de, x='log2FoldChange', y='pvalue', net=net, name=source, top=10)
dc.pl.source_targets(data=de, x='weight', y=stat_column, net=net, name=source, top=15, figsize=(4,4)) [weighted networks only]
dc.pl.leading_edge(de, stat=stat_column, net=net[net['weight'] > 0] and net[net['weight'] < 0], name=source) for weighted networks; net unsplit for unweighted

dc.pl.network(net=net, data=de[[stat]].T (row label = scores row), score=<scores CSV>, sources=network_sources or [source], targets=10, figsize=(5,5), vcenter=True, by_abs=True, size_node=10, t_label='Gene-level\nstatistic')

parameters.network_sources: optional list for the network plot; default [source]; tutorial cell 36 used ['SRF','MYOCD','IRF1','SKIL']
parameters.scores_path: optional wide scores CSV from tool 4 (full or significant; the tutorial passed the significant subset tf_acts). Network plot is skipped (listed in 'skipped') without it. All network_sources must be columns of it, else ValueError.
parameters.fixed: volcano top=10/y='pvalue', source_targets top=15, network targets=10 (tutorial values)

input_validation: DE CSV has log2FoldChange, pvalue, stat_column (numeric), unique gene index
source present in network (clear error instead of upstream assert)
at least one target of source measured in DE results
scores table has exactly one row
io_adaptations: data row label for dc.pl.network is set to the scores table's row label so upstream's same-index assertion holds
leading-edge gene arrays written as text (one gene per line, rank order)
a sign component with no measured targets is skipped and listed in 'skipped' instead of failing on upstream assert
decoupler_inspect_source_targets.outputs: <source>_targets_volcano.png, <source>_source_targets.png (weighted), <source>_leading_edge_<component>.png/.txt, <source>_network.png (with scores_path), <network>_network_used.csv; summary leading_edges {component: n_genes, first_genes (10), path}, n_targets_in_network, n_targets_measured, weighted_network, skipped, source_score (when in scores)
deviations: Leading-edge sign split applied to every network with a weight column (tutorial demonstrates it for PROGENy; CollecTRI weights are +/-1 so the same rule applies). Hallmark (no weights) gets one unsplit leading edge as in cell 60.

network_provenance.adaptation: Tools 4 and 5 accept network_path (CSV, TSV[.gz]/TXT[.gz] tab-separated, or Parquet) with source/target(/weight) columns; when given it is used instead of calling dc.op.<network>(organism='human'). The same dc.mt.ulm / dc.pl calls run on it; no method is added. Each call saves the table actually used as <network>_network_used.csv and returns network_origin (download call or absolute path) and network_rows.
network_provenance.why: CollecTRI (Zenodo), PROGENy (OmniPath) and Hallmark (static.omnipathdb.org) are live resources that drift; exact reference comparisons need the stage-2 snapshot.
network_provenance.csv_round_trip: Checked: read_csv of each snapshot CSV equals the parquet (sources/targets identical, weights bitwise equal).
network_provenance.note: The `network` Literal still selects plot presets and file names when network_path is given; the wrapper cannot verify that the file is that resource.

notes_for_verifier: Run with the executor snapshots via network_path for exact comparisons; pass contrast_name='treatment.vs.control' to match reference ulm table row labels.

Figures from dc.pl.volcano and dc.pl.source_targets use adjustText with a wall-clock limit, so label placement is not reproducible; compare data, not pixels. Tool PNGs are saved via savefig (savefig.dpi=150 from sc.set_figure_params), not the inline backend, so pixel comparison with notebooks/bulk_rna/images is not meaningful.

Metadata-input rule: condition labels come only from obs[condition_key]; the tool never creates or overwrites them. Relabelled-column/level tests (e.g. 'treatment_status' with 'TGFb'/'Ctrl') were not run by the implementer.

decoupler_score_activities_ulm and decoupler_inspect_source_targets download networks when network_path is omitted (hallmark download branch exercised once: 7318 rows, scores equal to snapshot on 2026-10-27).
PyDESeq2 runtime 28-80 s for this dataset; use generous MCP call timeouts.
